teams.heading: Fusi Feaunati appointed Head of Women's Rugby in Fiji, reports say
teams.body: The women's game has a new appointment: Fusi Feaunati has been appointed Head of Women's Rugby in Fiji, according to a report from Fiji Village. The men's job is still open, six months after Mick Byrne stepped down by mutual agreement on 1 April, and no successor has been announced. Jake White is among the names linked with the men's role, but no appointment has been reported.

teams.heading: Steve Borthwick's position strengthened after RFU review, contract since extended
teams.body: In a Guardian analysis from 1 October, Gerard Meagher argues Steve Borthwick's England remain full of contradictions a year before the World Cup. The RFU's public backing has swung hard: a vote of confidence after the historic Italy defeat read like an ultimatum, yet less than two months later a union review had strengthened his position. His contract was extended a few weeks before that piece, and Meagher notes the side's best performances come when players take matters into their own hands.

lead.why: The other shortlist items (Carpenter, Curry, Sleightholme) have already run on this tab, so this is the strongest remaining story about England's head coach.

teams.heading: Robert Kitson puts France's 1977 grand slam side first on inspiring list
teams.body: Robert Kitson's Guardian column of 6 October leads its proposed top six most inspiring rugby sides with France's 1977 Five Nations grand slam team. Kitson says that French team sheet "sent a shiver down the spine", placing it alongside the Pontypool pack of the late 1970s. The list rules out teams containing or coached by family members, and Kitson calls the exercise "entirely subjective".

lead.why: It is the only shortlist item with two outlets and not already covered by an earlier edition, and it is a France story rather than a Fiji or Wembanyama repeat.

teams.heading: Ireland women name WXV squad with Ruth Campbell back from ankle injury
teams.body: Ireland women have named Scott Bemand's squad for the WXV Global Series trip to Cape Town, with captain Erin King leading a group that includes Ruth Campbell, back from an ankle injury. Sam Monaghan remains out with an Achilles problem, and Aoife Wafer will not travel after missing the wins over Japan with what the IRFU called a "minor injury in training". The squad, announced on 9 October, faces the Springbok Women in Cape Town later this month.

teams.heading: Italy have conceded 318 points in their last 11 games
teams.body: Across their last 11 games, Italy have scored 190 points, an average of 17.3 a game. In the same window they have conceded 318, or 28.9 a game. Their biggest win over those 11 games is the 34-19 home victory over Chile in November 2025, an international friendly. The next fixture is South Africa, the reigning world champions.

teams.heading: Scottish Rugby takes charge of GB Sevens and reveals six new players
teams.body: Scottish Rugby has taken charge of Great Britain Sevens and revealed six new players for the squad. Test winger Hoyland has been given a sevens contract, and Scotland have allowed Bennett to pursue a place at the Rio Sevens. For Scotland, that makes the union responsible for the squad's direction and its players' pathways.

teams.heading: URC: Ellis Mee and Blair Murray press Tandy's case in Scarlets' win
teams.body: In URC round three, Scarlets came from 21-7 down at half-time to beat Benetton, and two Wales hopefuls did the heavy lifting. Murray was player of the match at full-back, a constant menace with ball in hand and a crucial interception, while Mee scored his second try with fast footwork. Mee started against Argentina and South Africa in July and, per BBC Sport Wales, has the nuts and bolts to stay in Steve Tandy's line-up before the Nations Championship squad is named on 20 October.

lead.why: A new Scarlets performance that bears directly on Steve Tandy's Wales selection, with the squad naming date still to come.

teams.heading: Argentina join Uruguay, Chile and Brazil in 2035 World Cup bid
teams.body: Reuters reported on 6 October that Argentina, Uruguay, Chile and Brazil have submitted a joint bid to host the 2035 World Cup, a multi-nation South American case rather than a single-country one. It comes as Los Pumas prepare for the 2027 tournament in Australia, where they are drawn with Fiji, Spain and Canada. Their next Test is Ireland in Round four of the Nations Championship.

lead.why: The Edwards and Aramburú stories have already run this week, and this bid is the only remaining item with a clear Argentina angle.

teams.heading: Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii rated a 'big disappointment' in Wallabies' Eden Park loss
teams.body: Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii's first Bledisloe Cup Test ended with Planet Rugby's player ratings calling him a 'big disappointment' in the 50-19 loss at Eden Park on Saturday. Les Kiss had kept him on the wing rather than move him back into midfield, persisting with the back three that beat South Africa in Perth. The Wallabies get their Sydney chance at Accor Stadium next Saturday.

lead.why: A player storyline on the Wallabies' side that the other Bledisloe pieces have not run, rather than another retelling of the defeat.

teams.heading: Japan women's sevens reclaim Asian Games gold, beating China 10-5 in final
teams.body: In early October at the Asian Games sevens in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan's women's side reclaimed the gold they last won two Games ago, edging defending champions China 10-5 in another tight final between the two. The Japan men's sevens side took bronze with a 17-5 win over Korea, who left the tournament without a medal for the first time. Hong Kong China's men completed a third straight gold.

lead.why: The strongest item not already reported: a women's sevens gold that a fan would still text about, even though it is a week old.

teams.heading: All Blacks retain Bledisloe Cup with 50-19 rout of Wallabies
teams.body: Saturday's first Bledisloe Test at Eden Park ended 50-19, with the All Blacks retaining the Bledisloe Cup and the Wallabies suffering a 12th straight defeat to New Zealand. Leading 17-14 at half-time, the hosts pulled away with five second-half tries, scored by Cam Roigard, Codie Taylor, Leroy Carter, Josh Moorby and Will Jordan. The result closes New Zealand's gap on South Africa at the top of the World Rugby rankings, 91.81 to the Springboks' 93.09, and a second Test follows next Saturday.

lead.why: The weekend's biggest result, and the Bledisloe story itself has not been led; the Barrett and Rennie angles have already run.

teams.heading: URC: Morné van den Berg's sin-bin cost Lions in 57-15 Bulls rout
teams.body: Springbok scrumhalf Morné van den Berg's sin-binning after 25 minutes changed last Saturday's URC match at Loftus Versfeld, reducing the Lions to 14 men as the Bulls led 31-10 at the break en route to a 57-15 win. Lions coach Ivan van Rooyen said the card was 'quite costly' and admitted his side were below par. The defeat was the Lions' first of the campaign, after home wins over Leinster and the Ospreys.

lead.why: A new Springbok storyline from the URC weekend that is separate from the Mbonambi hearing already covered.
